**Hydrogen – A Quick Reference to Its Key Properties**

| Category | Property | Typical Value / Description |
|----------|----------|-----------------------------|
| **Basic Identity** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| | State at STP | Gas (colorless, odorless, tasteless) |
| | Boiling point | –252.9 °C (−423.2 °F) |
| | Melting point | –259.2 °C (−434.6 °F) |
| | Density (gas, 0 °C, 1 atm) | 0.0899 g L⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume (ideal gas) | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Electron affinity | 0.754 eV |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV |
| | Second ionization energy | 27.211 eV |
| | Heat of formation (gas) | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard enthalpy of combustion | –285.83 kJ mol⁻¹ (to H₂O) |
| | Standard Gibbs free energy of formation | 0 kJ mol⁻¹ (by definition) |
| | Standard entropy (gas) | 130.68 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Heat capacity (gas, 25 °C) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Speed of sound in H₂ | ~1270 m s⁻¹ (at 20 °C) |
| | Refractive index (visible) | ~1.000132 |
| | Viscosity (gas, 25 °C) | 8.76 × 10⁻⁶ Pa·s |
| | Thermal conductivity (gas, 25 °C) | 0.180 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Magnetic susceptibility | Diamagnetic (–2.7 × 10⁻⁶ cm³ mol⁻¹) |
| | Dipole moment | 0 D (non‑polar) |
| | Rotational constant (H₂) | 60.853 cm⁻¹ |
| | Vibrational frequency (H₂) | 4401 cm⁻¹ |
| | Bond dissociation energy (H–H) | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Spectral lines | Lyman, Balmer, Paschen series (hydrogen atom); rotational/vibrational bands (H₂) |
| | Quantum mechanical ground state | 1s¹ (electron in 1s orbital) |
| | Nuclear spin | ½ (proton) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N |
| | Proton mass | 1.6726 × 10⁻²⁷ kg |
| | Deuteron mass | 3.3436 × 10⁻²⁷ kg |
| | Triton mass | 5.0089 × 10⁻²⁷ kg |
| | Half‑life of tritium | 12.32 years |
| | Radioactivity | Tritium is β⁻ emitter (Eₘₐₓ ≈ 18.6 keV) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ (at 25 °C) |
| | Solubility in ethanol | ~0.1 mol L⁻¹ |
| | Solubility in liquid metals | High (e.g., in iron, ~0.1 wt % at 1000 °C) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | None (no lone pairs) |
| | Chemical reactivity | Highly reactive; forms hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH₂) and acids (e.g., HCl, H₂SO₄) |
| | Combustion reaction | 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O (exothermic) |
| | Electrochemical potential (vs SHE) | 0 V (by definition) |
| | Standard electrode potential (H⁺/H₂) | 0 V |
| | Redox behavior | Can be oxidized to H⁺ (in acid) or reduced to H₂ (in electrolysis) |
| | Catalytic activity | Used as a reducing agent; hydrogenation catalyst (Pd, Pt, Ni) |
| | Role in biology | Essential for energy metabolism (ATP synthesis), signaling (hydrogen sulfide, H₂S) |
| | Role in astrophysics | Most abundant element; key in stellar nucleosynthesis (proton–proton chain, CNO cycle) |
| | Role in fusion research | Fuel for D–T fusion (tritium + deuterium) |
| | Environmental impact | Green fuel (water as only combustion product) |
| | Safety considerations | Extremely flammable; forms explosive mixtures with air (1–4 % H₂ in air) |
| | Storage methods | Compressed gas, cryogenic liquid, metal hydrides, chemical carriers (e.g., ammonia borane) |
| | Energy density | 120 MJ kg⁻¹ (mass basis) – highest among fuels; lower volumetric density (~0.01 kg L⁻¹) |
| | Isotopic enrichment | Deuterium used in NMR, neutron moderation; tritium used in fusion and radiolabeling |
| | Spectroscopic signatures | Lyman‑α line at 121.6 nm; Balmer‑α (Hα) at 656.3 nm; Raman shift for H₂ at ~4155 cm⁻¹ |
| | Quantum statistics | Bosonic (H₂) vs fermionic (protium) – influences heat capacity at low T |
| | Phase diagram | Only one solid phase (α‑H₂) at low T; no liquid phase at 0 K (melting point ~14 K) |
| | Critical point | Tc ≈ 33.2 K, Pc ≈ 1.3 MPa |
| | Van der Waals constants | a ≈ 0.244 L² bar mol⁻², b ≈ 0.0266 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusion coefficient (gas) | ~0.2 cm² s⁻¹ (at 25 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Mean free path (gas) | ~68 nm (at 25 °C, 1 atm) |
| | Speed of sound in liquid H₂ | ~1120 m s⁻¹ (at 20 K) |
| | Optical transparency | Transparent in visible; absorbs UV below 91.2 nm (ionization threshold) |
| | Magnetic resonance | Proton NMR (¹H) – 42.577 MHz/T; deuterium NMR (²H) – 6.536 MHz/T |
| | Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) | ¹H NMR widely used in chemistry, medicine (MRI) |
| | Hyperfine structure | ¹H hyperfine splitting ~1420 MHz (21 cm line) – key in radio astronomy |
| | Quantum tunneling | Significant in proton transfer reactions, e.g., in enzyme catalysis |
| | Thermodynamic stability | Most stable element; no stable heavier isotopes beyond tritium |
| | Role in cosmology | Residual primordial hydrogen from Big Bang nucleosynthesis; cosmic background radiation |
| | Role in planetary science | Dominant component of gas giants (Jupiter, Saturn) and icy bodies (comets) |
| | Role in materials science | Hydrogen embrittlement in metals; used in hydrogen storage materials |
| | Role in energy storage | Hydrogen economy concept – fuel cells, electrolyzers, storage tanks |
| | Role in environmental science | Greenhouse gas potential (though short atmospheric lifetime) |
| | Role in medicine | PET imaging (fluorine‑18 decays to positrons, similar to H₂⁺) |
| | Role in industry | Production of ammonia (Haber–Bosch), methanol, hydrogenation of fats, etc. |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Atomic simplicity**: One proton, one electron; the lightest element.
- **Isotopic diversity**: Protium (stable), deuterium (stable, used in NMR & fusion), tritium (radioactive, used in fusion & radiolabeling).
- **Physical extremes**: Lowest boiling/melting points of any element; extremely low density.
- **Chemical versatility**: Forms hydrides, acids, bases, and fuels; central to both biological and industrial chemistry.
- **Energy relevance**: Highest mass‑based energy density; key fuel for future clean energy (fuel cells, fusion).
- **Scientific importance**: Fundamental in quantum mechanics (hydrogen atom), astrophysics (stellar fusion), and cosmology (Big Bang nucleosynthesis).

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any specific property or application!
